annotations.description: With Psychic Frog (UB) and Quantum Riddler (3UU) in hand, plus two Force of Negations that need blue cards to exile, the player needs both blue and black mana. They already have an Island on the battlefield. Fetching a basic Plains provides white mana but doesn't help cast anything in their hand. Fetching Watery Grave (paying 2 life) would give access to black mana for Psychic Frog on turn 3, which is the most important early play. Alternatively, Hallowed Fountain could provide blue+white, but white isn't needed for anything in hand. The basic Plains is essentially a dead mana source since nothing in hand requires white mana, while black mana is critically needed for Psychic Frog.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Plains from Flooded Strand
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Watery Grave (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) to have access to black mana for casting Psychic Frog next turn, or fetch it tapped if life preservation is a concern. Even Undercity Sewers (enters tapped, gives U/B + surveil) would be better since it enables the black mana needed.

annotations.description: Discarded Force of Negation to pump Psychic Frog when Griselbrand is an uncastable 8-mana creature with no reanimation support. Force of Negation is a live spell that can be cast for free on the opponent's turn by exiling the remaining blue card (the other Force of Negation). Griselbrand provides zero value in hand with only 3 lands and no way to cheat it into play.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Force of Negation to Psychic Frog's pump ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard Griselbrand, which is a completely dead card with no realistic path to being cast or otherwise used, preserving the second Force of Negation for interaction

annotations.description: Discarding Force of Negation to pump Psychic Frog removes a key counterspell from hand. With only 3 cards in hand (Force of Negation, Griselbrand, Solitude), Force of Negation is the most flexible defensive card - it can counter noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. The opponent has no board presence yet, so the Frog is already likely to connect. Discarding Griselbrand (which is nearly uncastable at 8 mana with only 3 lands and no reanimation visible) would preserve the counterspell while still pumping the Frog. Griselbrand in the graveyard could even fuel Psychic Frog's flying ability later.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Force of Negation to pump Psychic Frog with a +1/+1 counter.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Griselbrand instead - it's effectively a dead card in hand with no way to cast or reanimate it, while Force of Negation provides critical free countermagic protection on the opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Discarding Griselbrand to pump Psychic Frog wastes one of the most powerful cards in the deck. With Watery Grave providing black mana, Griselbrand could potentially be a reanimation target or hard-cast threat later. Solitude, on the other hand, has already been used (two copies in graveyard) and while it provides removal via Evoke, discarding it to pump the Frog is more reasonable since it's a white card in a deck that seems to want blue/black resources. Griselbrand in the graveyard is only useful if there's a reanimation package, but even then, keeping it in hand preserves optionality. Solitude as a discard is better because it's less impactful as a card in hand when you only have 3 lands and no white card to pitch for evoke anyway (you'd need another white card which you don't have).
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Griselbrand to Psychic Frog's pump ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard Solitude instead, preserving Griselbrand as a potential win condition or reanimation target. Solitude without another white card to enable Evoke is harder to use, while Griselbrand represents a massive threat.

annotations.description: Discarding Solitude during the beginning of turn 4 (before combat) to pump Psychic Frog with a +1/+1 counter. Solitude is an extremely powerful card that can be evoked to exile a creature by pitching a white card, and it serves as the only remaining card in hand. While pumping the Frog is valuable, discarding the last card in hand means GPT4om Vorthos is now hellbent with no interaction available. However, with all three lands tapped and Solitude requiring a white card to evoke (and no other white cards in hand), the Solitude was effectively dead for its evoke mode. The question is whether holding it for a future hard-cast (at 5 mana) or as a potential evoke target later (if a white card is drawn) would be more valuable than the +1/+1 counter now. Given the opponent has an empty board and no cards visible, the aggressive pump to make Frog a 2/3 (or 3/4 with prior counters) for combat damage + card draw is reasonable, but going hellbent sacrifices future flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Solitude to Psychic Frog's ability to add a +1/+1 counter during beginning of turn 4.
annotations.betterLine: Consider holding Solitude as the last card in hand for future hard-casting or evoke potential. The Frog already connects for combat damage and draws a card, which could find better discard fodder. Maintaining at least one card in hand preserves options.

annotations.description: Exiling Griselbrand from the graveyard to give Psychic Frog flying is wasteful. Griselbrand is a powerful reanimation target that could potentially be brought back later. The graveyard contains less valuable cards like Polluted Delta, Flooded Strand, and Solitude that would be better exile fodder since they have little utility in the graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Force of Negation, Griselbrand, and Flooded Strand from graveyard to give Psychic Frog flying.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Force of Negation, Flooded Strand, and Flooded Strand (or Polluted Delta/Solitude) instead, preserving Griselbrand as a potential reanimation target.

annotations.description: Casting Ephemerate targeting Psychic Frog is suboptimal since Psychic Frog has no enter-the-battlefield ability. The flicker accomplishes nothing meaningful. Discarding Ephemerate to Psychic Frog's pump ability would give a +1/+1 counter, making it a bigger attacker that draws a card on combat damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ephemerate targeting Psychic Frog (a creature with no ETB ability)
annotations.betterLine: Activate Psychic Frog's discard ability, discarding Ephemerate to put a +1/+1 counter on it, then attack as a 2/3

annotations.description: Casting Faithful Mending in precombat main when Psychic Frog would connect unblocked (opponent has no creatures). Attacking first draws a card from Frog's combat damage trigger, giving more cards and better information for Faithful Mending's draw-then-discard.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Faithful Mending in precombat main phase before attacking with Psychic Frog
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Psychic Frog first (unblocked, draw a card), then cast Faithful Mending post-combat with an extra card in hand for better discard selection

annotations.description: Psychic Frog was given flying by exiling all three graveyard cards (Force of Negation, Ephemerate, Solitude), but the opponent has no creatures on the battlefield, meaning flying is unnecessary to connect in combat. Ephemerate in the graveyard could have had future value with creatures like Solitude if drawn again.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled all three graveyard cards to give Psychic Frog flying when there were no opposing creatures to block.
annotations.betterLine: Don't activate the flying ability when the opponent has no blockers. Keep Ephemerate and other cards in the graveyard for potential future use, and just attack with Psychic Frog on the ground.

annotations.description: Exiled Faithful Mending (which has flashback {1}{W}{U}) from the graveyard to give Psychic Frog flying, just to deal 1 damage. With 0 cards in hand, Faithful Mending's flashback would draw 2 cards and gain 2 life next turn, which is far more valuable than 1 point of flying damage against a 20-life opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Psychic Frog's flying ability, exiling all 3 graveyard cards including Faithful Mending to deal 1 flying damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't activate the flying ability. Save Faithful Mending in graveyard to flash back next turn (Plains + Island + Watery Grave = {1}{W}{U}) to draw 2 cards and gain 2 life, which is critical when hellbent with 0 cards in hand.

annotations.description: Llama4 Stoic discarded Whir of Invention, which is their best way to find and deploy Goblin Charbelcher at instant speed (and can use artifacts to help pay via Improvise). With no lands in play, the Charbelcher combo is their primary win condition, and Whir of Invention is the most powerful enabler to tutor for it at instant speed. Meanwhile, they have three copies of Thundertrap Trainer which are relatively low-impact creatures, and one of those would have been a much better discard choice.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Whir of Invention
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the three Thundertrap Trainers, preserving Whir of Invention as a powerful tutor that can find Charbelcher at instant speed with Improvise helping to reduce the mana cost.

annotations.description: Llama4 Stoic is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Goblin Charbelcher. While they have two copies, Charbelcher is their primary win condition in what appears to be a combo deck (with two Lotus Blooms suspended). Discarding a redundant Thundertrap Trainer would preserve both combo pieces. The Thundertrap Trainers are card selection creatures but with three copies in hand, one is easily expendable. Keeping both Charbelchers provides insurance against discard effects or if one gets countered.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goblin Charbelcher
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Thundertrap Trainer instead, preserving both copies of the win condition Goblin Charbelcher

annotations.description: Chose to exile Ephemerate (a useful rebound spell) instead of Undercity Sewers (a tapped land with no graveyard utility) as the third card for Psychic Frog's flying activation. Ephemerate has potential future value if a creature with ETB is drawn, while the tapped land is essentially worthless in the graveyard.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Ephemerate as the third card for Psychic Frog's flying ability
annotations.betterLine: Exile Undercity Sewers instead, preserving Ephemerate in the graveyard for potential future use or as better-quality graveyard fuel later

annotations.description: Goblin Charbelcher is Llama4 Stoic's primary win condition in what appears to be a Charbelcher combo deck. The deck likely runs few or no lands, making Charbelcher potentially lethal when activated. Discarding the only copy in hand (with one already in the graveyard) removes the main path to winning the game. While they have Tameshi, Reality Architect which could potentially return an artifact from the graveyard, that's a fragile multi-step plan requiring specific board conditions.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Goblin Charbelcher
annotations.betterLine: Discard a redundant Thundertrap Trainer (having 3 copies) or a second Tameshi, Reality Architect (legendary, so the second copy has diminished value). These are far less critical to the game plan than the deck's primary win condition.

annotations.description: Casting Faithful Mending during their own precombat main phase instead of waiting for the opponent's end step. With Psychic Frog already tapped and no other cards in hand, there's no benefit to casting it now. Waiting until the opponent's end step would keep all 4 mana open during the opponent's turn for any drawn interaction (counterspells, removal, etc.), and the drawn cards would still be available for the next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Faithful Mending during precombat main phase with no other plays available
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn, hold Faithful Mending for the opponent's end step to maximize mana availability during their turn and preserve options with drawn cards

annotations.description: Spell Snare is highly relevant in this matchup as it cleanly counters Psychic Frog (MV 2), the opponent's primary threat. Meanwhile, having three Thundertrap Trainers is redundant - casting all three is unlikely and they're just 1/2 bodies that dig for spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spell Snare
annotations.betterLine: Discard the third Thundertrap Trainer or the second Tameshi, Reality Architect (legendary, so only one can be on the battlefield). Spell Snare is efficient interaction against the opponent's key 2-mana threats.

annotations.description: Used Force of Negation instead of Disrupting Shoal to counter Teferi, Time Raveler (MV 3). Disrupting Shoal could counter it by exiling Tameshi, Reality Architect (a blue card with MV 3) from hand. Force of Negation is a more versatile and powerful counterspell that should be saved for future threats, especially since it can counter noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. Additionally, Force of Negation on your own turn may require hard-casting for {1}{U}{U} which is mana-intensive.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Force of Negation to counter Teferi, Time Raveler
annotations.betterLine: Cast Disrupting Shoal exiling Tameshi, Reality Architect (MV 3) to counter Teferi, preserving Force of Negation for a future opponent's turn threat where its free alternate cost is available.

annotations.description: Llama4 Stoic appears to be casting Disrupting Shoal targeting Teferi, Time Raveler when Force of Negation is already on the stack presumably targeting the same Teferi. This wastes both the Disrupting Shoal and the exiled Tameshi, Reality Architect (a powerful card that could bounce and recur artifacts from the graveyard, including the two Goblin Charbelchers there) for no additional effect.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Disrupting Shoal exiling Tameshi, Reality Architect to counter Teferi, Time Raveler while Force of Negation was already on the stack targeting the same spell.
annotations.betterLine: Let Force of Negation resolve and counter Teferi on its own, preserving both Disrupting Shoal and the very valuable Tameshi, Reality Architect in hand.

annotations.description: Exiled Faithful Mending (which has flashback) instead of keeping it in the graveyard. Force of Negation has no utility from the graveyard, while Faithful Mending can be cast via flashback for {1}{W}{U} to draw cards and gain life in future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Atraxa, Psychic Frog, and Faithful Mending, keeping Force of Negation in graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Atraxa, Psychic Frog, and Force of Negation, keeping Faithful Mending in graveyard for its flashback value.

annotations.description: Disrupting Shoal requires exiling a blue card with mana value equal to the target spell's mana value. Quantum Riddler has MV 5, but all cards in hand (3x Thundertrap Trainer, 1x Fallaji Archaeologist) have MV 2. Exiling a MV 2 card sets X=2, which cannot counter a MV 5 spell. This wastes the Disrupting Shoal and the exiled card for nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to cast Disrupting Shoal with alternative cost (exile a blue card from hand) targeting Quantum Riddler (MV 5) when no MV 5 blue cards are available in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Should not have cast Disrupting Shoal at all since it cannot counter Quantum Riddler. Save resources and try to find another answer, or accept the Riddler resolving and look for other ways to survive.

annotations.description: Quantum Riddler has mana value 5 (costs {3}{U}{U}), not 2. The player confused the Warp cost {1}{U} with the card's actual mana value. No card in hand had mana value 5, so Disrupting Shoal could never counter Quantum Riddler. This wasted both Disrupting Shoal and Fallaji Archaeologist (exiled) for absolutely nothing. At 1 life facing Psychic Frog, throwing away two cards is devastating.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Fallaji Archaeologist (MV 2) to Disrupting Shoal attempting to counter Quantum Riddler (MV 5), which cannot work since X=2 ≠ 5.
annotations.betterLine: Should not have cast Disrupting Shoal at all since no card in hand has mana value 5. Saving resources (the Shoal and the Archaeologist) could have been more useful - e.g., casting Fallaji Archaeologist as a blocker or saving Disrupting Shoal for a spell that actually has MV 2.
